newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - April 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - April 17.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A memorial to the victims of the October 14, 1973 uprising has been cast into doubt, with the minister in charge warning the project could touch off national disunity. The project is politically sensitive and can invite conflict, says Montri Danpaibul, University Affairs Minister, who claims to have received letters opposing a memorial. (BANGKOK POST)

- The Counter Corruption Commission (CCC) has uncovered details of unusual bank transactions by a senior official of the Commerce Ministry totalling 324.7 million baht, as part of its investigation into suspected irregularities in the sale of natural rubber. The investigation began a year ago under the Banharn government after the Rubber Organisation found that it did not have a buyer for a confirmed contract for its stock of rubber. (THE NATION)

- Prime Minister's Secretary-General Boonchong Weesommai is seeking help from the opposition to clear up the controversy caused by a newspaper report that a high ranking Cabinet member has a son-in-law who is also in the Cabinet. Boonchong says Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, in an effort to raise his image to the standard held by other international leaders, wants the opposition to identify the father and son-in-law. (THE NATION)

- The Cabinet will meet at a special session today to discuss ways to fund new development projects for fiscal 1998 under an environment of economic slowdown and an austere fiscal policy. The meeting will be closely watched by the business community and the financial market since the budget set for the next fiscal year will affect local interest rates and the economy during the latter part of this year and 1998. (THE NATION)

- Over-subscription of the Yankee bond issue has encouraged a decision by the Government to make a similar issue on an annual basis, says Thai Bankers Association Chairman and Siam Commercial Bank President Olarn Chaipravat. He quotes a deputy finance minister as saying that the Finance Ministry has resolved to issue $400-$500 million worth of Yankee bonds a year, with each batch carrying a maturity of 10 years. (BUSINESS DAY)
